tasks.short: Run the HR team of 13: set priorities, weekly stand-ups, unblock HRBPs, recruiters, payroll and L&D.

today.trigger: Monday team meeting, escalations by Teams and mail, month-close and hiring peaks.
steps: Read Power BI HR dashboard and open escalations in Outlook
Set the week's priorities per value stream with team leads
Review stuck cases (offers, verzuim files, payroll errors) one by one
Hold 1:1s and coach HRBPs on difficult manager cases
Report status to the management team
drudgery: Chasing status across AFAS, Recruitee and mail before each meeting
Rebuilding the same weekly status slide by hand
today.time_sinks: Gathering who-is-stuck-where across three sites and four systems eats most of Monday morning.

lenses.faster: A Monday brief built overnight from AFAS, Recruitee and Studytube lists stuck cases per value stream, so status gathering drops from hours to a 20-minute read; coaching and 1:1s stay as they are.
lenses.autonomous: The nightly AFAS extract triggers the brief and an exceptions list (offers older than 5 days, verzuim files near a poortwachter deadline); the Director only acts on the exceptions.
lenses.ambitious: Workload and priority calls made weekly per site instead of quarterly, so Venlo and Tilburg get explicit HR capacity during flex peaks; demand would grow as it gets cheaper because site managers ask for it.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses assembling the status slide; the Director wants more time coaching HRBPs and with site managers on the floor.
lenses.options: Two or three staffing plans for the team during peak season (shift recruiters to Venlo, or pool HR admin) change who does what, so drafts are worth comparing.
lenses.altitude: The week moves from chasing status to setting which HR agents run alone, which need review and who approves, with the logs to prove it; the job becomes more expert in operating-model design and AI governance.
reach: People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: maintaining the weekly team KPI view (needs basic Power BI modelling)
HR Business Partner: first triage of manager escalations

tasks.human_edge: Leading people: reading morale, coaching through hard cases, judging who can take on more, and holding accountability for the team's decisions.
tasks.pattern_why: Leadership work has no fixed steps; AI can prepare the brief, but the Director stays the lead in every decision.

in_practice.trigger: Nightly AFAS extract refresh before the Monday meeting.
steps: Pull open cases and deadlines from AFAS, Recruitee and Studytube
Draft a one-page brief of stuck cases per value stream and site
Director reviews and sets priorities in the meeting
Copilot drafts the MT status note from the agreed priorities
in_practice.human_gate: Director approves priorities and any reassignment of work; nothing goes to the MT unchecked.
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint HR team site, weekly brief archive

evidence.claim: HR platforms let the customer set which tasks run alone, which need review and when a person decides, logging every action with its approver.
Agent management is seen as a new HR job; governance is unsolved.
Status briefs from structured HR data are routine for current assistants.

risks: Brief becomes a performance monitoring tool for HR staff, which needs works council consent (WOR Art. 27)
Wrong data in the AFAS extract leads to wrong priorities
Director spends less time on the floor, not more
research_questions: How many hours a week does the Director spend gathering status today (diary for two weeks)?
Can AFAS, Recruitee and Studytube data be joined per case without manual keys?
Would the OR treat a case-level team brief as monitoring of employees?

tasks.short: Answer managers' policy questions (leave, conduct, harassment, equal treatment) and propose policy changes.

today.trigger: A manager mails, calls or walks in with a policy question or an incident.
steps: Clarify the situation with the manager
Look up the CAO article, internal policy on SharePoint or past cases
Give advice and, if needed, involve the HRBP or confidential adviser
Note recurring questions and propose a policy change to the MT and OR
drudgery: Answering the same leave and CAO questions every week
Searching old mails for how a similar case was handled
today.time_sinks: Routine CAO and leave questions crowd out the few sensitive cases that need the Director.

lenses.faster: Routine questions go to a policy desk that answers from the two CAOs and SharePoint policies with citations; the Director reviews only flagged or new answers, cutting this task by about 40%.
lenses.autonomous: A manager's question in Teams starts it; the desk drafts an answer with sources, sends low-risk answers from an approved set, and routes anything about harassment, discrimination, dismissal or medical data to an HRBP or the Director.
lenses.ambitious: Shift leaders on night shifts and in Venlo get a policy answer within minutes for the first time, instead of waiting until office hours; demand would grow as it gets cheaper.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses the tenth explanation of holiday carry-over; the Director wants more time on the sensitive cases and on fixing the policies that cause repeat questions.
lenses.options: For a policy change (say, a new rule on flex worker induction), two or three drafted variants with their CAO and OR implications change what goes to the works council.
lenses.altitude: The Director owns which question types the desk may answer alone, reviews its weekly log of escalations and turns repeat questions into policy changes; the role becomes more expert in policy design, less in answering.
reach: HR Business Partner: first-line policy questions from managers
HR Administrator: standard leave and contract questions

tasks.human_edge: Harassment, discrimination and conflict cases need judgement, trust and confidentiality; the Director weighs context and people, and carries accountability.
tasks.pattern_why: Questions arrive in unpredictable forms and need lookups across CAOs, policies and past answers; a person approves new or sensitive answers before they count.

in_practice.trigger: Manager posts a question in the HR Teams channel or mail.
steps: Classify the question and screen for sensitive topics
Retrieve CAO articles and SharePoint policies, draft answer with citations
Send pre-approved answer types directly; queue others for HRBP or Director review
Log question, answer and source; flag repeats for policy review
in_practice.human_gate: HRBP or Director approves any new answer type and every sensitive case; harassment and conflict go straight to a person.
data_needed: Current CAO Beroepsgoederenvervoer and warehouse CAO
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint list of questions, answers, sources and approver

evidence.claim: IBM's AskHR handled 16 million messages in 2025 at CSAT +74, after an earlier cut of human HR support drove internal NPS to −35.
At IBM India 90–95% of HR questions go through an assistant while managers keep decisions.
Chatbots must disclose that they are AI (AI Act Art. 50).

risks: Removing the human route too early, as IBM did
Wrong CAO citation creates a precedent or a claim
Sensitive case misclassified as routine
AVG breach if the desk sees medical or personal data
research_questions: What share of manager questions in the last three months were routine CAO or leave questions?
How accurate are cited answers on 50 real past questions, judged by an HRBP?
Does the OR want to discuss the desk under Art. 24 or does it need consent?

tasks.short: Dig into verzuim, turnover and 90-day retention data to find causes and propose policy fixes.

today.trigger: Monthly HR report, a spike in verzuim or early leavers at a site, or an MT question.
steps: Pull AFAS extracts or Power BI views
Slice in Excel by site, shift, team, contract type and agency
Form hypotheses and check with HRBPs and site managers
Write recommendations for the MT
drudgery: Re-cutting the same Excel pivots every month
Reconciling headcount between AFAS and agency portals
today.time_sinks: Data cleaning and slicing take most of the time; the thinking about causes gets squeezed.

lenses.faster: A copilot on the People Analyst's metric layer answers slicing questions in plain language and drafts the driver analysis, so the Director spends time on causes and fixes; about 45% saved.
lenses.autonomous: The nightly refresh runs fixed checks (verzuim above threshold per team, early leavers per agency or shift) and posts an alert with the likely drivers; the Director decides what to investigate.
lenses.ambitious: Monthly root-cause reviews per site and shift, including flex workers by agency for the first time, linked to the 90-day North Star; demand grows as it gets cheaper.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses the pivot tables; the Director wants more time talking to site managers about why people leave.
lenses.options: Comparing two or three explanations (shift pattern, team leader, onboarding gap) with the data for each changes which fix gets funded.
lenses.altitude: The Director sets which signals trigger an investigation and decides on interventions with the MT; the work becomes more expert in causal reasoning and less in spreadsheet work.
reach: People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: standard monthly reports
FP&A Analyst: cost of verzuim and turnover

tasks.human_edge: Knowing the sites, the team leaders and the history behind the numbers, and judging which cause is real and which fix the organisation will accept.
tasks.pattern_why: Analysis questions vary each month; the Director leads and the copilot does the slicing and drafting on a governed metric layer.

in_practice.trigger: Nightly Power BI refresh, monthly HR report, or a threshold alert.
steps: Run fixed threshold checks on verzuim, early leavers and onboarding completion
Copilot answers the Director's follow-up slices on the metric layer
Draft a short cause analysis with charts and caveats
Director checks with HRBPs and site managers and writes the recommendation
in_practice.human_gate: Director signs off conclusions before they reach the MT; no individual-level conclusions leave HR.
in_practice.logs_to: Power BI workspace and SharePoint analysis archive

evidence.claim: Natural-language querying of Power BI models and drafted narratives are standard features of current BI copilots.
The digest advises copilot on the people analyst's metric layer, scenarios rather than one number.

risks: Small teams make individuals identifiable (AVG)
Correlation read as cause
Monitoring of employees can become high-risk under the AI Act from Dec 2027 and needs OR consent
research_questions: Is the AFAS extract clean enough on site, shift and agency to support driver analysis?
Do agency portals give leaver data on flex workers that can be joined?
Which past recommendations were acted on, and did the metric move?

tasks.short: Plan the HR year: training programme, CAO talks, OR agenda, recruitment campaigns, across three sites.

today.trigger: Annual planning, CAO calendar, OR meeting cycle, seasonal peaks.
steps: Collect needs from site managers and HR leads
Draft the HR year plan and training calendar in Excel
Align with the OR, Finance and the transport and warehouse CAO timelines
Track progress and adjust each month
drudgery: Merging plans from many mails into one Excel
Chasing owners for monthly progress updates
today.time_sinks: Coordination across sites and parties (OR, unions, Finance) takes far longer than the planning itself.

lenses.faster: A copilot merges site inputs into a draft plan, keeps the action list current from Teams and mail, and drafts OR and MT updates; about 20% saved.
lenses.autonomous: Calendar milestones (CAO end 31 Dec 2026, OR meetings, certificate expiries in Studytube) trigger reminders and draft agendas; the Director decides content.
lenses.ambitious: An AI-literacy and AI-policy track agreed with the OR and offered to all 1,200 staff including night shifts, which FNV now asks for at the CAO table; demand grows as it gets cheaper.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses chasing progress updates; the Director wants more time preparing the CAO round and the OR relationship.
lenses.options: Two or three versions of the training budget split (forklift and VCA renewals versus leadership versus AI literacy) change what is decided.
lenses.altitude: The Director's year plan includes the AI rules: which agents HR runs, their gates, and the OR agreements behind them; the role grows in labour relations and governance expertise.
reach: Learning and Development Specialist: draft annual training calendar from Studytube expiries
HR Business Partner: site-level plan consolidation

tasks.human_edge: Negotiating trade-offs with the OR, unions and site managers, and sequencing change so the organisation accepts it.
tasks.pattern_why: Planning is iterative and political; the copilot drafts and tracks, the Director leads.

in_practice.trigger: Annual planning cycle and monthly progress review.
steps: Collect site inputs via a Teams form
Copilot drafts the year plan and training calendar from inputs and Studytube expiries
Director reviews with MT and OR
Monthly, copilot drafts the progress update from the action list
in_practice.human_gate: Director approves the plan and every OR or union communication.
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint HR plan and action list

evidence.claim: Works council should discuss AI policy in the Art. 24 meeting; some decisions need advice or consent.
FNV asks for worker zeggenschap over AI and AI-literacy training at the CAO table.
The transport CAO runs to 31 Dec 2026.
The employer must take AI-literacy measures under the AI Act.

risks: Plan looks complete on paper but site managers did not commit
AI-literacy track seen as a cost without OR buy-in
research_questions: How much of planning time is coordination versus drafting today?
Does the OR want a joint AI agreement before the 2027 CAO round?
Can Studytube export expiries per site reliably?

tasks.short: Build and track the HR budget: headcount costs, flex, training, recruitment, from AFAS and CAO tables.

today.trigger: Annual budget round with Finance and monthly cost reports.
steps: Export positions and salaries from AFAS to Excel
Apply CAO increases, pension changes and step raises by hand
Add flex worker, recruitment and training budgets
Agree with the Finance Director and Controller
Compare actuals monthly and explain variances
drudgery: Applying CAO scales and step raises in Excel per employee
Reconciling agency invoices against hours for the variance report
today.time_sinks: Rebuilding the salary model every year and explaining flex variances.

lenses.faster: A rules-based model computes personnel cost from AFAS positions, CAO tables and pension rules, so the Director reviews assumptions and variances instead of building sheets; about 50% saved.
lenses.autonomous: Month close in AFAS triggers the actuals-versus-budget run and a variance list with agency invoice matches; the Director explains only flagged variances.
lenses.ambitious: Cost every CAO union demand in the 2027 round within a day, so the bargaining team can test offers during talks instead of after; demand grows as it gets cheaper.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses per-person CAO step calculations; the Director wants more time on the trade-offs with Finance.
lenses.options: Scenarios for the CAO outcome (wage rise of 3, 4 or 5%, pension switch timing) and flex-versus-permanent mixes change the budget decision.
lenses.altitude: The Director owns the budget assumptions and the scenarios shown to the MT; the work becomes more expert in labour cost economics.
reach: FP&A Analyst: personnel cost line of the company forecast
Compensation and Benefits Specialist: CAO increase calculations

tasks.human_edge: Choosing assumptions, negotiating the budget with the Finance Director and judging which costs to defend.
tasks.pattern_why: Salary scales, CAO increases and pension rules can be written down; built fast with AI coding, it runs without a model.

in_practice.trigger: Budget round start and AFAS month close.
steps: Load positions and salaries from the AFAS extract
Apply CAO tables, step raises and pension rules
Add flex, recruitment and training lines from agency and Studytube data
Produce budget, scenarios and monthly variance list
in_practice.human_gate: Director and Finance Director approve the assumptions and the final budget.
systems: Excel or a small Python model
data_needed: CAO wage tables and pension rules
in_practice.logs_to: Versioned model and assumptions file on SharePoint

evidence.claim: The digest recommends deterministic software from AFAS positions and CAO tables at autonomy 3.
Workday's Work Intelligence cut a planned 50 hires to 42 in a demo, showing task-based cost planning.

risks: Wrong CAO rule coded silently spreads across all lines
Model not maintained after the 2027 CAO and pension switch
Agency data not consistent across three portals
research_questions: How many hours do the Director and Controller spend on the personnel budget today?
Can agency portals export hours and rates in a stable format?
Does the model match last year's actual payroll within 1%?

tasks.short: Keep up with labour law, court rulings and both CAOs, and tell the MT what it means for us.

today.trigger: New legislation, CAO results, rulings, newsletters from lawyers and employer bodies.
steps: Read newsletters, CAO texts and rulings
Mark what applies to Noordhaven
Write short notes for the MT, HRBPs and payroll
Update policies on SharePoint when needed
drudgery: Skimming many newsletters that mostly do not apply
Comparing old and new CAO texts by hand
today.time_sinks: Reading volume; most items turn out irrelevant.

lenses.faster: A model call summarises each new item with citations and a relevance tag for Noordhaven (transport, warehouse, flex, verzuim), and diffs CAO versions; the Director reads a weekly digest and checks sources; about 55% saved.
lenses.autonomous: New items in subscribed sources trigger a summary and relevance check; only items tagged relevant reach the Director's weekly digest.
lenses.ambitious: A monthly briefing for HRBPs, payroll and site managers on what changed and what they must do, a service they do not get today; demand would grow.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses skimming irrelevant newsletters; the Director wants more time on what a change means for strategy and the CAO round.
lenses.options: Little; summaries do not change the decision, but two readings of an ambiguous rule can be shown side by side.
lenses.altitude: The Director reads less and decides more about which changes to act on; the expertise shifts to interpretation and labour law strategy.
reach: HR Business Partner: legal updates to managers
Payroll Specialist: impact notes on CAO wage table changes

tasks.human_edge: Interpreting what an ambiguous ruling or CAO clause means for Noordhaven and when to call the labour lawyer.
tasks.pattern_why: One model call turns a messy document into a checkable summary with citations inside a fixed weekly flow.

in_practice.trigger: New item from a subscribed source or new CAO text.
steps: Fetch new items from chosen sources
Summarise with citations and tag relevance
Diff CAO versions article by article
Compile a weekly digest for the Director
in_practice.human_gate: Director checks cited sources before anything is shared or a policy changes.
data_needed: Source list (government, employer bodies, unions, law firms)

evidence.claim: Summaries of legislation and CAOs with citations at autonomy 3 are suggested in the digest.
Recruitment, task allocation, monitoring, evaluation and termination systems become high-risk from 2 Dec 2027, a change this monitoring would track.

risks: Summary misses a nuance or invents a citation
Over-reliance replaces legal advice where it is needed
research_questions: On 20 past items, does the summary match what the Director concluded?
Which sources cover Dutch transport and warehouse labour law best?
How often does a missed item cause a later problem today?

tasks.short: Oversee job descriptions and grading so roles fit the CAO scales fairly.

today.trigger: New role, reorganisation, appeal against a grading, CAO change.
steps: Collect the job description from the manager
Compare with the CAO function grid and reference jobs
Agree the grade with the Compensation Specialist
Handle appeals with the grading committee
drudgery: Rewriting vague job descriptions into the CAO format
Finding the closest reference job by hand
today.time_sinks: Back-and-forth with managers on job content.

lenses.faster: A copilot rewrites the manager's input into the CAO format and suggests the closest reference jobs with reasons; the Director and specialist decide; about 30% saved.
lenses.autonomous: A new role request in AFAS triggers the draft description and reference job match; the grading itself stays with people.
lenses.ambitious: A yearly check of all warehouse roles against the grid, so drift in what people actually do (new scanning tasks, robots) is caught for the first time; demand grows modestly.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses rewriting vague descriptions; the Director wants more time on fairness and pay-equity questions.
lenses.options: Two or three grading proposals with their cost and CAO arguments help in appeals and reorganisations.
lenses.altitude: The Director owns a consistent grading method and the pay-equity view; the role becomes more expert in job architecture.
reach: Compensation and Benefits Specialist: first-draft grading proposals
HR Business Partner: job description drafting with managers

tasks.human_edge: Judging job content against the CAO in disputed cases, and handling appeals fairly and visibly to employees and the OR.
tasks.pattern_why: Grading needs judgement; the copilot drafts and compares, people decide; it rates jobs, not people.

in_practice.trigger: New or changed role request in AFAS or by mail.
steps: Draft description in CAO format from manager input
Suggest closest reference jobs with reasons
Specialist and Director agree the grade
Record grade and rationale in AFAS
in_practice.human_gate: Director or grading committee decides every grade and appeal.
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS job record and SharePoint grading archive

evidence.claim: The digest recommends copilot at autonomy 2, rating jobs not people.
Evaluation of people can be high-risk under the AI Act from Dec 2027; rating jobs is outside that scope if no person is scored.

risks: Suggestion bias anchors the grade
Tool drifts into rating individuals, which changes the legal status
Appeals rise if staff see AI in grading
research_questions: How many gradings and appeals happen per year?
Does the warehouse CAO grid have a usable reference job library?
Does the OR need to be consulted on AI use in grading?

tasks.short: Forecast how many drivers, warehouse staff and flex workers we need per site next year.

today.trigger: Annual budget, new customer contracts, seasonal peaks.
steps: Get volume plans from operations
Translate into FTE per site and shift in Excel
Add expected leavers, retirements and verzuim
Split permanent versus flex and agree with Finance
drudgery: Rebuilding the FTE model per site each year
Guessing leaver rates without clean history
today.time_sinks: Getting volume assumptions from operations and rebuilding the model.

lenses.faster: A standing model links volume plans to FTE with historic leaver and verzuim rates from AFAS, and a copilot builds scenarios on request; about 40% saved.
lenses.autonomous: A new volume plan or customer contract triggers a recalculation and a gap list per site and shift; the Director decides hiring and flex mix.
lenses.ambitious: A quarterly hiring and flex plan per site agreed with the three agencies in advance, instead of last-minute orders in peak; demand grows as it gets cheaper.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses rebuilding the Excel model; the Director wants more time on the permanent-versus-flex strategy.
lenses.options: Scenarios (volume plus or minus 15%, a new customer in Venlo, higher verzuim) change hiring decisions, not just effort.
lenses.altitude: The Director sets workforce strategy with operations and Finance from scenarios; the role becomes more expert in workforce planning.
reach: FP&A Analyst: FTE side of the operations forecast
Recruiter: annual hiring plan per site

tasks.human_edge: Judging which volume assumptions to trust and how far to rely on flex workers given CAO, agency and labour market limits.
tasks.pattern_why: The arithmetic can be fixed in a model, but choosing scenarios and assumptions needs the Director; the copilot builds and explains them.

in_practice.trigger: Volume plan update or budget round.
steps: Load volume plans and AFAS history
Compute FTE need per site and shift with leaver and verzuim rates
Copilot builds three scenarios with gaps
Director agrees the plan with operations and Finance
in_practice.human_gate: Director approves the forecast and hiring plan.

evidence.claim: Workday Work Intelligence (beta) cut a planned 50 hires to 42 in a demo.
AFAS Profit 8 computes a candidate match score for vacancies and internal talent.

risks: Forecast quality limited by operations' volume plans
False precision in one number instead of scenarios
research_questions: How far off were the last two forecasts per site?
Do operations have productivity norms per role and shift?
Can agency fill rates be pulled from the three portals?

role.altitude: From running HR services to designing Noordhaven's HR operating system: which agents run alone, where the gates are, what is logged, and the works council and CAO agreements that back it.
reach: HR Business Partner: routine manager policy questions via the policy desk
FP&A Analyst: personnel cost lines and CAO scenario costing
People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: standard monthly HR reports
Compensation and Benefits Specialist: CAO increase calculations
role.ceiling_note: About 30% of the Director's 1,600 hours could be freed, mostly in policy questions, analysis, legal reading and budgets; leadership, OR and union relations, hearings and sensitive cases stay human, and the AI Act high-risk rules from Dec 2027 limit how far recruitment and evaluation tools can go.
skills_to_grow: AI governance: setting autonomy levels, gates and logs per agent
AI Act and works council compliance (Art. 50, high-risk annex, WOR Art. 24/27)
Scenario-based workforce and labour cost planning
Prompting and checking AI output with citations
role.ambitious_version: Make Noordhaven the first in its sector to agree AI rules with the OR and unions in the 2027 CAO round, with an HR policy desk serving night shifts and flex workers at all three sites, and costed scenarios for every union demand during talks.
